hints.title: Cross-Half Subarray Pair Counting
hints.text: Counting reverse pairs directly takes quadratic time. How can divide and conquer count cross-half pairs while sorting subarrays?

hints.title: Sorted Halves Monotonic Pointer Invariant
hints.text: Since both left and right subarrays are independently sorted, a monotonic index scans right elements satisfying the condition without backtracking.

hints.title: Merge Sort Cross Inversion Counting Procedure
hints.text: Apply merge sort recursively. Before merging two sorted halves, advance an index j in the right half for each element i in the left half to count pairs where nums[i] exceeds two times nums[j]. Merge the sorted halves and return accumulated pair count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing all pairs (i, j) requires O(N^2) time, which is too slow for arrays with up to 50,000 integers.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Merge sort recursion computes the count in O(N log N) time using O(N) auxiliary array space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle 64-bit integer overflow when multiplying nums[j] by 2 and advance the comparison pointer monotonically in linear time per merge.
